cards.title: Pharaoh Ordering Haman to Bake Clay Bricks and Build a Tower to Heaven
cards.note: Surah 28:38–42 portrays Pharaoh in Egypt ordering Haman to bake clay bricks and build a lofty tower to climb to the God of Moses, combining the baked-brick tower of Babel (Genesis 11:3–4; Sanhedrin 109a) with Haman from the Persian court of Esther 3:1.

discussion.view: Muslim commentators and modern harmonizers propose that Haman was either an unrecorded Egyptian court minister or a title of an Egyptian quarry official distinct from the Persian vizier in the Book of Esther.
discussion.reply: In the Hebrew Bible, Haman the Agagite serves King Ahasuerus (Xerxes) in fifth-century BC Persia (Esther 3:1), roughly a millennium after Moses and Pharaoh in New Kingdom Egypt. Furthermore, firing clay bricks in a kiln to build a tower reaching the heavens is the specific architectural motif of Mesopotamia's Tower of Babel in Genesis 11:3–4 rather than Egyptian stone masonry.

cards.quranEn: [38] Pharaoh said, ‘Assembly! I know of no other god for you than me. So light a fire for me, Haman, on the clay, and make a tower for me, so that I may look at the god of Moses. Surely I think he is indeed one of the liars.’ [39] He and his forces became arrogant on the earth without any right, and thought that they would not be returned to Us. [40] So We seized him and his forces, and tossed them into the sea. See how the end was for the evildoers! [41] We made them leaders (who) call (others) to the Fire, and on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped. [42] We pursued them in this world with a curse, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be among the scorned.
quranHighlights: Pharaoh said, ‘Assembly! I know of no other god for you than me. So light a fire for me, Haman, on the clay, and make a tower for me, so that I may look at the god of Moses.

cards.title: Talut (Saul) Testing Troops at the River Like Gideon Before Slaying Goliath
cards.note: Surah 2:249–251 attributes to King Talut (Saul) the river-drinking test of Gideon's army from Judges 7:4–7—separating those who drink freely from those who scoop water by hand—immediately before David slays Jalut (Goliath) as in 1 Samuel 17:48–51.

discussion.view: Muslim commentators explain this passage either as a separate unrecorded test conducted by King Saul on the march to face Goliath or as an intentional prophetic parallel between two Israelite campaigns.
discussion.reply: In the Hebrew Bible, the river test separating three hundred men who scoop water with their hands from the rest of the army belongs to the judge Gideon fighting the Midianites (Judges 7:4–7). King Saul's campaign against the Philistines and David's slaying of Goliath occur generations later in 1 Samuel 17, where no river-drinking test takes place.

cards.quranEn: [249] When Ṭālūt set out with his forces, he said, ‘Surely God is going to test you by means of a river. Whoever drinks from it is not on my side, but whoever does not taste it is surely on my side, except for whoever scoops (it) up with his hand.’ But they (all) drank from it, except for a few. So when he crossed it, he and those who believed with him, they said, ‘We have no strength today against Jālūt and his forces.’ But those who thought that they would meet God said, ‘How many a small cohort has overcome a large cohort by the permission of God? God is with the patient.’ [250] So when they went forth to (battle) Jālūt and his forces, they said, ‘Our Lord, pour out on us patience, and make firm our feet, and help us against the people who are disbelievers.’ [251] And they routed them by the permission of God, and David killed Jālūt, and God gave him the kingdom and the wisdom, and taught him about whatever He pleased. If God had not repelled some of the people by means of others, the earth would indeed have been corrupted. But God is full of favor to the worlds.

cards.title: Combining the Unblemished Red Cow and the Heifer for an Unsolved Murder
cards.note: Surah 2:67–73 merges two distinct Torah statutes into one narrative: the unblemished, unworked cow of Numbers 19:2–3 and the unworked heifer slaughtered for an unknown homicide in Deuteronomy 21:1–4, adding that striking the corpse revives the victim.

discussion.view: Classical commentators such as al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir recount an Israelite inheritance murder in which God commanded the sacrifice of a specific golden-yellow cow so that striking the slain man with its bone or flesh would bring him back to name his killer.
discussion.reply: In the Pentateuch, Numbers 19:2–9 prescribes burning an unblemished, unworked red cow to produce purification ashes for corpse-contamination, while Deuteronomy 21:1–9 prescribes breaking the neck of an unworked heifer in a valley to absolve a town of an unsolved murder. Neither statute involves striking a corpse with the cow to resurrect the victim.

cards.quranEn: [67] (Remember) when Moses said to his people, ‘Surely God commands you to slaughter a cow.’ They said, ‘Do you take us in mockery?’ He said, ‘I take refuge with God from being one of the ignorant.’ [68] They said, ‘Call on your Lord for us, so that He may make clear to us what it (should be).’ He said, ‘Surely He says, “Surely it is to be a cow, not old and not young, (but) an age between that.” Do what you are commanded!’ [69] They said, ‘Call on your Lord for us, so that He may make clear to us what color it (should be).’ He said, ‘Surely He says, “Surely it is to be a yellow cow, its color bright, delighting to the onlookers.”’ [70] They said, ‘Call on your Lord for us, so that He may make clear to us what (kind) it (should be). Surely cows are all alike to us. And surely (then), if God pleases, we shall indeed be (rightly) guided.’ [71] He said, ‘Surely He says, “Surely it is to be a cow, not broken in to plough the earth or to water the field, (but one that is) sound, without any blemish on it.”’ They said, ‘Now you have brought the truth.’ So they slaughtered it, though they nearly did not. [72] (Remember) when you killed a man, and you argued about it, but God brought forth what you were concealing. [73] So We said, ‘Strike him with part of it.’ In this way God brings the dead to life, and shows you His signs so that you may understand.

cards.quranAr: وَإِذۡ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوۡمِهِۦٓ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأۡمُرُكُمۡ أَن تَذۡبَحُواْ بَقَرَةٗۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَتَتَّخِذُنَا هُزُوٗاۖ قَالَ أَعُوذُ بِٱللَّهِ أَنۡ أَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡجَٰهِلِينَ ﴿67﴾ قَالُواْ ٱدۡعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّن لَّنَا مَا هِيَۚ قَالَ إِنَّهُۥ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٞ لَّا فَارِضٞ وَلَا بِكۡرٌ عَوَانُۢ بَيۡنَ ذَٰلِكَۖ فَٱفۡعَلُواْ مَا تُؤۡمَرُونَ ﴿68﴾ قَالُواْ ٱدۡعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّن لَّنَا مَا لَوۡنُهَاۚ قَالَ إِنَّهُۥ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٞ صَفۡرَآءُ فَاقِعٞ لَّوۡنُهَا تَسُرُّ ٱلنَّـٰظِرِينَ ﴿69﴾ قَالُواْ ٱدۡعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّن لَّنَا مَا هِيَ إِنَّ ٱلۡبَقَرَ تَشَٰبَهَ عَلَيۡنَا وَإِنَّآ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَمُهۡتَدُونَ ﴿70﴾ قَالَ إِنَّهُۥ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٞ لَّا ذَلُولٞ تُثِيرُ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَلَا تَسۡقِي ٱلۡحَرۡثَ مُسَلَّمَةٞ لَّا شِيَةَ فِيهَاۚ قَالُواْ ٱلۡـَٰٔنَ جِئۡتَ بِٱلۡحَقِّۚ فَذَبَحُوهَا وَمَا كَادُواْ يَفۡعَلُونَ ﴿71﴾ وَإِذۡ قَتَلۡتُمۡ نَفۡسٗا فَٱدَّـٰرَ ٰٔتُمۡ فِيهَاۖ وَٱللَّهُ مُخۡرِجٞ مَّا كُنتُمۡ تَكۡتُمُونَ ﴿72﴾ فَقُلۡنَا ٱضۡرِبُوهُ بِبَعۡضِهَاۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يُحۡيِ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰ وَيُرِيكُمۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَعۡقِلُونَ ﴿73﴾

cards.title: Mary Accused by Her People and Addressed as Sister of Aaron
cards.note: In Surah 19:27–28, Mary's people accuse her over her child and address her as 'Sister of Aaron' ('daughter of Imran' in 66:12), combining Protevangelium of James 15 with Miriam, sister of Aaron and daughter of Amram, in Exodus 15:20 and Numbers 26:59.

discussion.view: Muslim traditions (Sahih Muslim 2135) and classical commentators explain that Mary was called 'Sister of Aaron' either figuratively after a righteous Israelite man or because she belonged to the Levitical lineage of Aaron.
discussion.reply: In Hebrew and Arabic (`Maryam`), Mary Mother of Jesus and Miriam of the Exodus share the same name. The Quran calls Jesus's mother both 'Sister of Aaron' (19:28) and 'daughter of Imran' (66:12; 3:35), matching the biblical family triad of Miriam—daughter of Amram (`Imran`) and sister of Aaron in Numbers 26:59 and Exodus 15:20—who lived over a millennium before first-century Mary.

cards.title: Noah Remaining Among His People Nine Hundred and Fifty Years Before the Flood
cards.note: Surah 29:14–15 states that Noah stayed among his people 'a thousand years minus fifty years' (950 years) before the Flood, assigning Noah's 950-year total lifespan from Genesis 9:29 to his pre-Flood mission instead of the 600 years of Genesis 7:6.

discussion.view: Classical commentators such as Ibn Abbas (in al-Tabari) and Ibn Kathir explain that Noah preached to his people for 950 years before the Flood and lived additional centuries afterward.
discussion.reply: In Genesis 7:6 and 9:28–29, Noah is 600 years old when the Flood begins, lives 350 years after the Flood, and dies at a total age of 950 years. Surah 29:14 retains the exact biblical number 950 ('a thousand years minus fifty years') while placing the entire 950-year span prior to the Flood.

cards.quranEn: [14] Certainly We sent Noah to his people, and he stayed among them a thousand years, minus fifty years, and then the flood seized them while they were doing evil. [15] But We rescued him and (his) companions on the ship, and made it a miracle for all peoples.

cards.title: Pharaoh Boasting to Moses: Do Not These Rivers of Egypt Flow Beneath Me
cards.note: Surah 43:46–56 places into the mouth of the Exodus Pharaoh confronting Moses the boast 'Is the kingdom of Egypt not mine, and these rivers which flow beneath me,' attributing to him Pharaoh Hophra's Nile boast in Ezekiel 29:2–3.

discussion.view: Muslim commentators explain that Rameses or the Pharaoh of the Exodus boasted before his assembly of Egypt's Nile canals and tributaries to belittle Moses prior to the drowning in the Red Sea.
discussion.reply: In the Hebrew Bible, the Pharaoh of the Exodus confronts Moses by the Nile (Exodus 5:2; 7:15), whereas the specific boast 'The rivers are mine, and I made them' belongs to Pharaoh Hophra (Apries, r. 589–570 BC) in Ezekiel 29:2–3 and 29:9, more than six centuries after the Exodus.

cards.quranEn: [46] Certainly We sent Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his assembly. He said, ‘Surely I am a messenger of the Lord of the worlds.’ [47] But when he brought them Our signs, suddenly they began to laugh at them, [48] even though every sign We showed them was greater than the one before it. We seized them with the punishment, so that they might return. [49] They said, ‘Magician! Call on your Lord for us by whatever covenant He has made with you, (and) surely we shall indeed be (rightly) guided.’ [50] But when We removed the punishment from them, immediately they broke (their promise). [51] Pharaoh called out among his people: ‘My people! Is the kingdom of Egypt not mine, and these rivers (which) flow beneath me? Do you not see? [52] Am I not better than this (man), who is despicable and scarcely makes (things) clear? [53] If only bracelets of gold were cast (down) on him or the accompanying angels came with him.’ [54] So he unsettled his people, and they obeyed him. Surely they were a wicked people. [55] When they had angered Us, We took vengeance on them and drowned them – all (of them)! [56] We made them a thing of the past, and an example for the later (generations).
quranHighlights: Certainly We sent Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his assembly.
Pharaoh called out among his people: ‘My people! Is the kingdom of Egypt not mine, and these rivers (which) flow beneath me?

sources.title: Septuagint (LXX2012) - Ezekiel
sources.en: Son of man, set your face against Pharao king of Egypt, and prophesy against him, and against the whole of Egypt: and say, Thus says the Lord; Behold, I am against Pharao, the great dragon that lies in the midst of his rivers, that says, The rivers are mine, and I made them.
highlights: Behold, I am against Pharao, the great dragon that lies in the midst of his rivers, that says, The rivers are mine, and I made them.

cards.quranAr: وَلَقَدۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا مُوسَىٰ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ إِلَىٰ فِرۡعَوۡنَ وَمَلَإِيْهِۦ فَقَالَ إِنِّي رَسُولُ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ ﴿46﴾ فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُم بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ إِذَا هُم مِّنۡهَا يَضۡحَكُونَ ﴿47﴾ وَمَا نُرِيهِم مِّنۡ ءَايَةٍ إِلَّا هِيَ أَكۡبَرُ مِنۡ أُخۡتِهَاۖ وَأَخَذۡنَٰهُم بِٱلۡعَذَابِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَرۡجِعُونَ ﴿48﴾ وَقَالُواْ يَـٰٓأَيُّهَ ٱلسَّاحِرُ ٱدۡعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ بِمَا عَهِدَ عِندَكَ إِنَّنَا لَمُهۡتَدُونَ ﴿49﴾ فَلَمَّا كَشَفۡنَا عَنۡهُمُ ٱلۡعَذَابَ إِذَا هُمۡ يَنكُثُونَ ﴿50﴾ وَنَادَىٰ فِرۡعَوۡنُ فِي قَوۡمِهِۦ قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ أَلَيۡسَ لِي مُلۡكُ مِصۡرَ وَهَٰذِهِ ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِيٓۚ أَفَلَا تُبۡصِرُونَ ﴿51﴾ أَمۡ أَنَا۠ خَيۡرٞ مِّنۡ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِي هُوَ مَهِينٞ وَلَا يَكَادُ يُبِينُ ﴿52﴾ فَلَوۡلَآ أُلۡقِيَ عَلَيۡهِ أَسۡوِرَةٞ مِّن ذَهَبٍ أَوۡ جَآءَ مَعَهُ ٱلۡمَلَـٰٓئِكَةُ مُقۡتَرِنِينَ ﴿53﴾ فَٱسۡتَخَفَّ قَوۡمَهُۥ فَأَطَاعُوهُۚ إِنَّهُمۡ كَانُواْ قَوۡمٗا فَٰسِقِينَ ﴿54﴾ فَلَمَّآ ءَاسَفُونَا ٱنتَقَمۡنَا مِنۡهُمۡ فَأَغۡرَقۡنَٰهُمۡ أَجۡمَعِينَ ﴿55﴾ فَجَعَلۡنَٰهُمۡ سَلَفٗا وَمَثَلٗا لِّلۡأٓخِرِينَ ﴿56﴾

cards.title: Parable of the Boastful Vineyard Owner Whose Lush Estate Is Ruined
cards.note: Surah 18:32–44 portrays a rich man boasting over two hedged grape gardens before his harvest is ruined overnight, combining Jesus' Parable of the Rich Fool in Luke 12:16–21 with the hedged vineyard laid waste in Isaiah 5:1–6.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir report from early exegetes that the parable of the two garden owners in 18:32–44 illustrates a believer and a disbeliever among the ancients (often identified as two brothers among the Israelites) to warn Mecca's wealthy elite.
discussion.reply: The Quranic parable merges two canonical biblical passages: Isaiah 5:1–6, where a fertile vineyard hedged and planted with choice vines is laid waste when rain is withheld, and Luke 12:16–21, where a rich landowner boasts to his soul over his stored harvest on the very night his life and estate are stripped away.

cards.quranEn: [32] Strike for them a parable of two men: We made for one of them two gardens of grapes, and surrounded both with date palms, and placed between them (a field of) crops. [33] Each of the two gardens produced its fruit and did not fail in any way. And We caused a river to gush forth between them. [34] And he had fruit. So he said to his companion, while he was talking with him, ‘I am greater than you in wealth, and mightier in family.’ [35] And he entered his garden, doing himself evil, (for) he said, ‘I do not think that this will ever perish, [36] nor do I think the Hour is coming. If indeed I am returned to my Lord, I shall indeed find a better (place of) return than this.’ [37] His companion said to him, while he was talking with him, ‘Do you disbelieve in Him who created you from dust, then from a drop, (and) then fashioned you as a man? [38] But as for us, He is God, my Lord, and I do not associate anyone with my Lord. [39] Why did you not say, when you entered your garden, “What God pleases,” (for there is) no power except in God? If you see me as inferior to you in wealth and children, [40] it may be that my Lord will give me (something) better than your garden, and send on it a reckoning from the sky, so that it becomes slippery soil, [41] or its water sinks (into the earth), so that you will not be able to find it.’ [42] And (all) his fruit was overwhelmed, and in the morning he began wringing his hands over what he had spent on it, (for) it had collapsed on its trellises, and he said, ‘I wish I had not associated anyone with my Lord!’ [43] But there was no cohort to help him, other than God, and he was helpless. [44] In such a case protection (belongs only) to God, the True One. He is best in reward, and best in final outcome.

And he entered his garden, doing himself evil, (for) he said, ‘I do not think that this will ever perish
And (all) his fruit was overwhelmed, and in the morning he began wringing his hands

sources.title: Gospel of Luke (NASB)
sources.en: And He told them a parable, saying, "The land of a rich man was very productive. "And he began reasoning to himself, saying, 'What shall I do, since I have no place to store my crops?' "Then he said, 'This is what I will do: I will tear down my barns and build larger ones, and there I will store all my grain and my goods. 'And I will say to my soul, "Soul, you have many goods laid up for many years [to come]; take your ease, eat, drink [and] be merry."' "But God said to him, 'You fool! This [very] night your soul is required of you; and [now] who will own what you have prepared?' "So is the man who stores up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God."

sources.title: Book of Isaiah (Septuagint LXX)
sources.en: And I made a hedge round it, and dug a trench, and planted a choice vine, and built a tower in the midst of it, and dug a place for the wine-vat in it: and I waited [for it] to bring forth grapes, and it brought forth thorns. And now, you⌃ dwellers in Jerusalem, and [every] man of Juda, judge between me and my vineyard. What shall I do any more to my vineyard, that I have not done to it? And now I will tell you what I will do to my vineyard: I will take away its hedge, and it shall be for a spoil; and I will pull down its walls, and it shall be [left] to be trodden down. cards.quranAr: ۞وَٱضۡرِبۡ لَهُم مَّثَلٗا رَّجُلَيۡنِ جَعَلۡنَا لِأَحَدِهِمَا جَنَّتَيۡنِ مِنۡ أَعۡنَٰبٖ وَحَفَفۡنَٰهُمَا بِنَخۡلٖ وَجَعَلۡنَا بَيۡنَهُمَا زَرۡعٗا ﴿32﴾ كِلۡتَا ٱلۡجَنَّتَيۡنِ ءَاتَتۡ أُكُلَهَا وَلَمۡ تَظۡلِم مِّنۡهُ شَيۡـٔٗاۚ وَفَجَّرۡنَا خِلَٰلَهُمَا نَهَرٗا ﴿33﴾ وَكَانَ لَهُۥ ثَمَرٞ فَقَالَ لِصَٰحِبِهِۦ وَهُوَ يُحَاوِرُهُۥٓ أَنَا۠ أَكۡثَرُ مِنكَ مَالٗا وَأَعَزُّ نَفَرٗا ﴿34﴾ وَدَخَلَ جَنَّتَهُۥ وَهُوَ ظَالِمٞ لِّنَفۡسِهِۦ قَالَ مَآ أَظُنُّ أَن تَبِيدَ هَٰذِهِۦٓ أَبَدٗا ﴿35﴾ وَمَآ أَظُنُّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ قَآئِمَةٗ وَلَئِن رُّدِدتُّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّي لَأَجِدَنَّ خَيۡرٗا مِّنۡهَا مُنقَلَبٗا ﴿36﴾ قَالَ لَهُۥ صَاحِبُهُۥ وَهُوَ يُحَاوِرُهُۥٓ أَكَفَرۡتَ بِٱلَّذِي خَلَقَكَ مِن تُرَابٖ ثُمَّ مِن نُّطۡفَةٖ ثُمَّ سَوَّىٰكَ رَجُلٗا ﴿37﴾ لَّـٰكِنَّا۠ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ رَبِّي وَلَآ أُشۡرِكُ بِرَبِّيٓ أَحَدٗا ﴿38﴾ وَلَوۡلَآ إِذۡ دَخَلۡتَ جَنَّتَكَ قُلۡتَ مَا شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِٱللَّهِۚ إِن تَرَنِ أَنَا۠ أَقَلَّ مِنكَ مَالٗا وَوَلَدٗا ﴿39﴾ فَعَسَىٰ رَبِّيٓ أَن يُؤۡتِيَنِ خَيۡرٗا مِّن جَنَّتِكَ وَيُرۡسِلَ عَلَيۡهَا حُسۡبَانٗا مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَتُصۡبِحَ صَعِيدٗا زَلَقًا ﴿40﴾ أَوۡ يُصۡبِحَ مَآؤُهَا غَوۡرٗا فَلَن تَسۡتَطِيعَ لَهُۥ طَلَبٗا ﴿41﴾ وَأُحِيطَ بِثَمَرِهِۦ فَأَصۡبَحَ يُقَلِّبُ كَفَّيۡهِ عَلَىٰ مَآ أَنفَقَ فِيهَا وَهِيَ خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَىٰ عُرُوشِهَا وَيَقُولُ يَٰلَيۡتَنِي لَمۡ أُشۡرِكۡ بِرَبِّيٓ أَحَدٗا ﴿42﴾ وَلَمۡ تَكُن لَّهُۥ فِئَةٞ يَنصُرُونَهُۥ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا كَانَ مُنتَصِرًا ﴿43﴾ هُنَالِكَ ٱلۡوَلَٰيَةُ لِلَّهِ ٱلۡحَقِّۚ هُوَ خَيۡرٞ ثَوَابٗا وَخَيۡرٌ عُقۡبٗا ﴿44﴾

cards.title: Pharaoh Commanding Haman to Build a Tower to the Ropes of the Heavens
cards.note: In Surah 40:36–37, Pharaoh orders Haman to build a tower (sarhan) to reach the 'ropes of the heavens' (asbab al-samawat) and look upon Moses' God, merging Genesis 11:3–4 (Babel), Esther 3:1 (Haman), and the aerial castle of the Story of Ahikar.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explain that Pharaoh commanded his vizier Haman to construct a high brick tower in Egypt so Pharaoh could ascend toward the pathways of the sky and test Moses' claim regarding the God of heaven.
discussion.reply: Unlike 28:38, which specifies baking clay bricks, 40:36–37 focuses on reaching the 'ropes of the heavens' (asbab al-samawat). The passage merges three ancient traditions separated by centuries: the Tower of Babel built to reach heaven in Genesis 11:3–4, the Persian court minister Haman under King Artaxerxes in Esther 3:1, and Pharaoh's demand for a castle between heaven and earth in the Story of Ahikar.

cards.quranEn: [36] Pharaoh said, ‘Haman! Build a tower for me, so that I may reach the ropes, [37] the ropes of the heavens, and look upon the god of Moses. Surely I think he is a liar indeed.’ In this way the evil of his deed was made to appear enticing to Pharaoh, and he was kept from the way. But the plot of Pharaoh only (came) to ruin.
quranHighlights: Pharaoh said, ‘Haman! Build a tower for me, so that I may reach the ropes,
the ropes of the heavens, and look upon the god of Moses.

cards.title: Mary Styled 'Daughter of 'Imran' (Amram of Numbers 26:59)
cards.note: Surah 66:12 directly calls Mary, the mother of Jesus, 'Mary, daughter of 'Imran' (Maryama bnata 'Imrana), assigning to her the patronymic of Miriam, daughter of Amram and sister of Aaron and Moses in Numbers 26:59.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explain that 66:12 names Mary 'daughter of 'Imran' either after her biological father from the Davidic or priestly line, or by ancestral lineage to the Mosaic 'Imran (Amram), while Gabriel breathed into the sleeve of her garment.
discussion.reply: Whereas 19:28 addresses Mary as 'sister of Aaron' and 3:35 speaks of the 'wife of 'Imran,' 66:12 explicitly names Mary 'daughter of 'Imran' (Maryama bnata 'Imrana). In the Hebrew Bible and Septuagint (Numbers 26:59; Exodus 6:20), Amram ('Imran) is the Levitical father of Aaron, Moses, and their sister Miriam (Greek Mariam), thirteen centuries before Jesus' mother Mary (whose father in early Christian tradition is Joachim).

cards.quranEn: And Mary, daughter of ‘Imrān, who guarded her private part: We breathed into it some of Our spirit, and she affirmed the words of her Lord and His Books, and became one of the obedient.

cards.title: Qarun, Pharaoh, and Haman Grouped as Arrogant Opponents of Moses
cards.note: Surah 29:39–40 groups Qarun (Korah), Pharaoh, and Haman together as recipients of Moses' clear signs who acted arrogantly on earth before being destroyed by earth-swallowing and drowning, combining Numbers 16:1–3 and Esther 3:1.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explain that in 29:39–40 Moses brought clear signs to Pharaoh, his vizier Haman, and the wealthy Israelite Qarun in Egypt, after which God caused the earth to swallow Qarun (28:81) and drowned Pharaoh, Haman, and their hosts in the sea.
discussion.reply: In the Hebrew Bible, Korah (Qarun) is an Israelite Levite who rebels against Moses in the Sinai wilderness after the Exodus (Numbers 16:1–3), whereas Haman the Agagite is a fifth-century BC Persian courtier under King Artaxerxes in Susa (Esther 3:1). Talmud Bavli Sanhedrin 110a connects Korah's wealth to Joseph's buried treasures in Egypt, explaining how Korah came to be linked with Pharaoh's court.

cards.quranEn: [39] And Qārūn, and Pharaoh, and Haman – certainly Moses brought them the clear signs, but they became arrogant on the earth. Yet they did not outrun (Us). [40] We seized each one for his sin. We sent a sandstorm against one of them, and another of them was seized by the cry, and We caused the earth to swallow (yet) another of them, and We drowned (still) another of them. Yet God was not one to do them evil, but they did themselves evil.
quranHighlights: And Qārūn, and Pharaoh, and Haman – certainly Moses brought them the clear signs
We caused the earth to swallow (yet) another of them, and We drowned (still) another of them

cards.quranAr: وَقَٰرُونَ وَفِرۡعَوۡنَ وَهَٰمَٰنَۖ وَلَقَدۡ جَآءَهُم مُّوسَىٰ بِٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتِ فَٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا كَانُواْ سَٰبِقِينَ ﴿39﴾ فَكُلًّا أَخَذۡنَا بِذَنۢبِهِۦۖ فَمِنۡهُم مَّنۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِ حَاصِبٗا وَمِنۡهُم مَّنۡ أَخَذَتۡهُ ٱلصَّيۡحَةُ وَمِنۡهُم مَّنۡ خَسَفۡنَا بِهِ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَمِنۡهُم مَّنۡ أَغۡرَقۡنَاۚ وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيَظۡلِمَهُمۡ وَلَٰكِن كَانُوٓاْ أَنفُسَهُمۡ يَظۡلِمُونَ ﴿40﴾

cards.title: Pharaoh Slaughtering Israelite Sons Beside Haman and Their Hosts in Egypt
cards.note: Surah 28:3–6 recounts Pharaoh slaughtering Israelite sons while sparing their women, and pairs Haman and his forces (Fir'awna wa-Hamana wa-junudahuma) directly with Pharaoh during the Exodus 1 infanticide, combining Exodus 1:16–22 and Esther 3:1–6.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir identify Haman in 28:6 as Pharaoh's chief minister and advisor in Egypt during the oppression of the Israelites, distinguishing him from the Persian Haman of the Book of Esther or treating the name as an Egyptian court title.
discussion.reply: In Exodus 1:16–22 and Talmud Bavli Sotah 12a, Pharaoh decrees that newborn Hebrew males be cast into the Nile without any minister named Haman. Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite appears a millennium later in Esther 3:1–6 as the grand vizier of the fifth-century BC Persian king Artaxerxes/Ahasuerus in Susa who plotted to exterminate the Jews of the Persian Empire.

cards.quranEn: [3] We recite to you some of the story of Moses and Pharaoh in truth, for a people who believe: [4] Surely Pharaoh had exalted himself on the earth, and divided its people (into) parties, weakening one contingent of them (by) slaughtering their sons and sparing their women. sources.en: And after this king Artaxerxes highly honored Aman [son] of Amadathes, the Bugaean, and exalted him, and set his seat above all his friends. And all in the palace did him obeisance, for so the king had given orders to do: but Mardochaeus did not do him obeisance. And they in the king's palace said to Mardochaeus, Mardochaeus, why do you transgress the commands of the king? [Thus] they spoke daily to him, but he listened not to them; so they represented to Aman that Mardochaeus resisted the commands of the king: and Mardochaeus had shown to them that he was a Jew. And when Aman understood that Mardochaeus did not obeisance to him, he was greatly enraged, and took counsel to destroy utterly all the Jews who were under the rule of Artaxerxes.

cards.title: Moses Sent to Pharaoh, Haman, and Qarun and Defended by a Royal Believer
cards.note: Surah 40:23–29 sends Moses to Pharaoh, Haman, and Qarun (40:24) and introduces a believer from Pharaoh's house who warns the royal council that if Moses is truthful God's punishment will strike them (40:28), matching Sotah 11a and Acts 5:34–39.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explain that Moses was sent to Pharaoh, his minister Haman, and the wealthy Israelite Qarun in Egypt, while a Coptic kinsman of Pharaoh who secretly believed spoke up in the royal assembly to dissuade Pharaoh from executing Moses.
discussion.reply: Surah 40:23–29 combines two distinct elements: first, 40:24 groups Egypt's Pharaoh with Haman (the Persian courtier of Esther 3:1) and Qarun/Korah (an Israelite Levite whose Egyptian treasure keys are described in Talmud Sanhedrin 110a); second, 40:28 puts on the lips of a royal advisor the conditional warning of Gamaliel before the Sanhedrin in Acts 5:38–39 alongside Pharaoh's advisors in Sotah 11a.

cards.quranEn: [23] Certainly We sent Moses with Our signs and clear authority [24] to Pharaoh, and Haman, and Qārūn, but they said, ‘A magician, a liar!’ [25] When he brought them the truth from Us, they said, ‘Kill the sons of those who believe with him, and keep their women alive.’ Yet the plot of the disbelievers always goes astray. [26] Pharaoh said, ‘Let me kill Moses, and let him call on his Lord. Surely I fear that he will change your religion, or that he will cause corruption to appear on the earth.’ [27] Moses said, ‘I take refuge with my Lord and your Lord from every arrogant one (who) does not believe in the Day of Reckoning.’ [28] A (certain) man, a believer from the house of Pharaoh, (who) concealed his belief, said, ‘Will you kill a man because he says, “My Lord is God,” when he has brought you the clear signs from your Lord? If he is a liar, his lie is on him, but if he is truthful, some of what he promises you will smite you. Surely God does not guide anyone who is wanton (and) a liar. [29] My people! Today the kingdom (belongs) to you (who) prevail on the earth, but who will help us against the violence of God, if it comes upon us?’ Pharaoh said, ‘I only show you what I see, and I only guide you to the right way.’

sources.title: Talmud Bavli, Sotah 11a
sources.ref: Talmud Bavli Sotah 11a (Pharaoh's Counsel Against Israel and the Three Royal Advisors)
sources.en: Three noteworthy people were consulted by Pharaoh in that counsel where Pharaoh questioned what should be done with the Jewish people. They were Balaam, and Job, and Yitro. Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba teaches what occurred to each of them: Balaam, who advised Pharaoh to kill all sons born to the Jewish people, was punished by being killed in the war with Midian (see Numbers 31:8). Job, who was silent and neither advised nor protested, was punished by suffering, as detailed in the eponymous book in the Bible. Yitro, who ran away as a sign of protest.
highlights: Three noteworthy people were consulted by Pharaoh in that counsel where Pharaoh questioned what should be done with the Jewish people.
Balaam, who advised Pharaoh to kill all sons born to the Jewish people
Yitro, who ran away as a sign of protest

cards.quranAr: وَلَقَدۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا مُوسَىٰ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا وَسُلۡطَٰنٖ مُّبِينٍ ﴿23﴾ إِلَىٰ فِرۡعَوۡنَ وَهَٰمَٰنَ وَقَٰرُونَ فَقَالُواْ سَٰحِرٞ كَذَّابٞ ﴿24﴾ فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُم بِٱلۡحَقِّ مِنۡ عِندِنَا قَالُواْ ٱقۡتُلُوٓاْ أَبۡنَآءَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مَعَهُۥ وَٱسۡتَحۡيُواْ نِسَآءَهُمۡۚ وَمَا كَيۡدُ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ إِلَّا فِي ضَلَٰلٖ ﴿25﴾ وَقَالَ فِرۡعَوۡنُ ذَرُونِيٓ أَقۡتُلۡ مُوسَىٰ وَلۡيَدۡعُ رَبَّهُۥٓۖ إِنِّيٓ أَخَافُ أَن يُبَدِّلَ دِينَكُمۡ أَوۡ أَن يُظۡهِرَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ ٱلۡفَسَادَ ﴿26﴾ وَقَالَ مُوسَىٰٓ إِنِّي عُذۡتُ بِرَبِّي وَرَبِّكُم مِّن كُلِّ مُتَكَبِّرٖ لَّا يُؤۡمِنُ بِيَوۡمِ ٱلۡحِسَابِ ﴿27﴾ وَقَالَ رَجُلٞ مُّؤۡمِنٞ مِّنۡ ءَالِ فِرۡعَوۡنَ يَكۡتُمُ إِيمَٰنَهُۥٓ أَتَقۡتُلُونَ رَجُلًا أَن يَقُولَ رَبِّيَ ٱللَّهُ وَقَدۡ جَآءَكُم بِٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتِ مِن رَّبِّكُمۡۖ وَإِن يَكُ كَٰذِبٗا فَعَلَيۡهِ كَذِبُهُۥۖ وَإِن يَكُ صَادِقٗا يُصِبۡكُم بَعۡضُ ٱلَّذِي يَعِدُكُمۡۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهۡدِي مَنۡ هُوَ مُسۡرِفٞ كَذَّابٞ ﴿28﴾ يَٰقَوۡمِ لَكُمُ ٱلۡمُلۡكُ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ ظَٰهِرِينَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَمَن يَنصُرُنَا مِنۢ بَأۡسِ ٱللَّهِ إِن جَآءَنَاۚ قَالَ فِرۡعَوۡنُ مَآ أُرِيكُمۡ إِلَّا مَآ أَرَىٰ وَمَآ أَهۡدِيكُمۡ إِلَّا سَبِيلَ ٱلرَّشَادِ ﴿29﴾
